Evidence quotes, distractors, grammatical alternatives and visible bounds were author-self-reviewed. Frozen source IDs supply matching level/form only. No independent teacher validation, learner calibration or publication is claimed.

units.title: 初二语法：奖杯照片下面的姓名

materials.title: Trophy Photo Names
materials.text:
Our sports club wanted a photograph of the team with an old school trophy. The teacher ____1____ (BRING) it from a cupboard last Tuesday and placed it on a table. She asked us ____2____ (CHECK) the names written on the display card.

One player ____3____ had joined the team in September was missing from the card. He had not played in the final match, but he had trained with us every week. We discussed whether the caption should describe the final team or all the club members.

The teacher listened ____4____ (PATIENT) while we explained our different ideas. In the end, we made two captions. One identified the players in the final, and the other named everyone in ____5____ (WE) training group.

After ____6____ (TAKE) the photograph, we checked that each person could be seen. The picture was ____7____ (WIDE) than the first one because more people stood beside the table. We did not try to make one caption answer two different questions.

The trophy went back ____8____ the cupboard before the room was used for another lesson. We kept a copy of both captions with the photograph.

questions.explanation: last Tuesday过去brought谓语。
ask somebody to do不定式。
player作定从主语who/that。
修饰listened用patiently。
training group前物主our。
After介词后taking动名词。
than比较wider。

questions.prompt: Gap 8: Refer to the inside of the cupboard. Write one word.
questions.explanation: back into/in/to cupboard均可表达回橱中，onto指顶面与from inside保管语境不同。

units.title: 初二语法：钟楼参观中的一次等待

materials.title: Bell Tower Listening
materials.text:
Last summer, our class visited a bell tower in the old part of town. A guide ____1____ (MEET) us at the entrance and asked us ____2____ (LEAVE) large bags in a locked room downstairs.

The stairs were narrower ____3____ we had expected. We went up in a small group and stopped at a window. The guide showed us the building ____4____ had once been the town's main school.

At the top, we waited ____5____ (QUIET) for the bell. It did not ring immediately. The guide explained that our visit had begun a few minutes before the hour, so we had time to look at the mechanism through a glass panel.

After ____6____ (HEAR) the bell, we wrote down what we had noticed. Some pupils described the movement, while others described the sound. Neither account told the whole story by ____7____ (IT).

Before leaving, we collected our bags and thanked the guide. Back at school, the teacher asked ____8____ we had learned that could not be found just by looking at a photograph of the tower.

questions.explanation: Last summer过去met谓语。
asked us to leave不定式。
narrower than比较。
building作had been主语，which/that。

questions.prompt: Gap 5 (QUIET): Use the adverb ending in -ly. Write one word.
questions.explanation: 修饰waited用quietly，题面指定-ly。
After介词后hearing。
by itself固定独自，Neither account单数。
what作learned宾语，引导间接问题。

units.title: 初二语法：借来的植物图册

materials.title: Garden Book Return
materials.text:
I borrowed a plant guide from our local library last month because our class was planning a garden. The librarian ____1____ (SHOW) me two books. One had detailed photographs, and the other explained how ____2____ (CHOOSE) plants for different conditions.

I took the second book. It was less colourful, but it answered the question ____3____ mattered most to our group: which plants could grow in a shady corner? My friend wanted to copy a picture from the first book without checking that point.

We read the guide ____4____ (CAREFUL) and made a short list. The corner was ____5____ (DARK) than the open area near the gate, so the same choice might not work in both places.

Before ____6____ (RETURN) the book, I checked every page for the paper markers we had used. I found one beside a useful table and copied the page number into ____7____ (WE) notebook. I did not leave the marker inside.

Next week, we plan ____8____ (ASK) the gardener about our list. The book has helped us prepare better questions, even though it cannot choose everything for our particular garden.

questions.explanation: last month过去showed。
how to do疑问词不定式。
question作mattered主语which/that。
修饰read用carefully。
than比较darker。
before介词后returning。
notebook前our。
plan to do不定式。

units.title: 初二语法：捐书前的书页检查

materials.title: Donation Book Pages
materials.text:
Our class collected books for a new reading corner last Friday. Before accepting a book, the teacher ____1____ (ASK) us to check its pages. A clean cover did not always mean that the book was complete.

I found a storybook ____2____ had two pages missing near the end. Its owner had not noticed the problem because she had read it a long time before. We did not put it in the box for younger readers, who might be confused by the missing part.

The teacher helped us decide what ____3____ (DO) with incomplete books. Some could be used for an art activity, but they needed to be kept separate ____4____ the books ready for reading. We wrote a clear note on each box.

After ____5____ (FINISH) the checks, we counted the accepted books. There were fewer ____6____ we had expected, yet every one could be opened and read from beginning to end.

We carried the boxes ____7____ (SLOW) to the new corner. The teacher thanked ____8____ (WE) for taking time over a job that seemed simple. The next class would not have to discover the missing pages by accident.

questions.explanation: last Friday过去asked谓语。
storybook作had主语，which/that。
what to do疑问词加不定式。
keep separate from与……分开。
After介词后finishing。
fewer than比较。
carried boxes slowly常规副词，slow也可平义副词，不误拒；明显错误词形另列。
thanked后宾格us。

units.title: 初二语法：广播节目里的姓名发音

materials.title: Radio Name Practice
materials.text:
Our school radio club invited a new teacher to talk about her home town. Before the interview, the producer ____1____ (SEND) her a list of questions. He also asked her ____2____ (RECORD) her name so the presenter could practise saying it.

The presenter, ____3____ was my classmate, listened to the short file several times. She did not assume that the name sounded like an English word with similar letters. The teacher helped her find the part ____4____ she had been stressing incorrectly.

During the interview, the teacher spoke ____5____ (CLEAR) about a festival in her town. We asked one question at a time and gave her enough time to answer. The conversation was longer ____6____ the programme could include.

After ____7____ (LISTEN) to the whole recording, we chose a shorter section and asked the teacher to approve it. We also checked the spelling of the place names in ____8____ (WE) written introduction.

The final programme sounded relaxed, but it had needed careful preparation. Knowing how to ask a question included knowing how to address the person who would answer it.

questions.explanation: 采访前寄问题可过去或过去完成。
ask somebody to do不定式。
逗号非限制定从指presenter，用who。
part作stressing宾语，which/that。
修饰spoke用clearly。
longer than比较。
After介词后listening。
introduction前our。

units.title: 初二语法：市场上称水果的秤

materials.title: Market Fruit Weighing
materials.text:
On our class visit to the town market, a fruit seller ____1____ (LET) us watch how she weighed an order. She placed an empty bowl on the scales before adding any apples. Then she showed us ____2____ the display changed when the bowl was included.

The seller asked us ____3____ (COMPARE) the weight of the fruit with and without its container. The apples were the same, but the total was ____4____ (HIGH) when the bowl was counted too. It was a simple way to show why a number needed a clear meaning.

A classmate ____5____ had brought a notebook drew the two displays. We wrote down what each number included instead of copying only the larger one. The seller checked our notes ____6____ (CAREFUL).

After ____7____ (BUY) some fruit for lunch, we thanked her and moved away from the stall so customers could be served. Back at school, we explained the example in ____8____ (WE) own words. We did not need to invent a new order or change the recorded weights.

questions.explanation: 过去let不规则仍let，letted在该义不标准。
showed how说明变化方式，showed that展示发生变化事实均可；what不能作完整从句缺口。
asked us to compare不定式。

questions.prompt: Gap 4 (HIGH): Use the comparative adjective. Write one word.
questions.explanation: 与不含容器对比，题面明确要求比较级higher。
classmate作从句主语who/that。
修饰checked用carefully。
after介词后buying。
own words前our。

units.title: 初三阅读：营地里没有换掉的帐篷

materials.title: Camp Tent Repair
materials.text:
Before our school camp, each group checked a borrowed tent. Ours had a small tear near the entrance. I wanted to choose another tent immediately, but the equipment leader asked us to record the problem first. The tear might be repairable, and simply moving it to the back of the store would leave the next group with the same surprise.

We photographed the damaged area and showed it to a member of staff. She said that the tent should not be used until the repair had been checked. We labelled the bag clearly and borrowed another tent for the trip. Nobody was asked to test the damaged one by sleeping in it.

After the camp, our group returned to help sort the equipment. The repaired tent was on a separate table with a note describing the work. The staff member checked it before removing the temporary label. I realised that the label had not been a judgement that the tent was worthless. It had explained its current condition and stopped an unfinished job from becoming invisible.

Our group wrote a return note for the tent we had used too. A clear record helped people after us, whether the news was a fault or simply that the equipment had been checked.

questions.prompt: Why did the equipment leader ask for a record before changing tents?
options: To avoid telling any adult about it.
To leave useful information for the next group.
To make the tear larger.
To ensure the damaged tent was used immediately.
questions.explanation: B正确：记录避免下一组同样意外；C不扩大损坏；A向工作人员报告；D检查前不用。

questions.prompt: What happened to the damaged tent before the trip?
options: It was taken on the trip for an overnight test.
It was secretly put at the back of the store.
It was labelled and another tent was borrowed.
It was given to a visitor without explanation.
questions.explanation: C正确：明确标袋另借一顶；B正避免藏后面；A无人试睡；D非送客。

questions.prompt: When was the temporary label removed?
options: When the narrator decided it looked attractive.
Before any repair work began.
As soon as the photograph was taken.
After a staff member checked the repaired tent.
questions.explanation: D正确：修后工作人员核查再去标签；C拍照未修；B修前不去；A非外观喜好。

questions.prompt: What did the narrator learn about the label?
options: It proved that every borrowed tent was broken.
It was only decoration for the bag.
It meant the tent could never be useful again.
It described the condition and kept unfinished work visible.
questions.explanation: D正确：标签说明现状防未完工隐没；C非永无价值；B非装饰；A非全坏证据。

questions.prompt: Why did the group also write about the tent it had used?
options: They wanted to replace the campsite’s rules.
The staff had lost every tent bag.
A useful return record includes checked equipment as well as faults.
Only damaged equipment could be returned.
questions.explanation: C正确：记录无论故障或已核均助后来人；D完整也还；B没丢所有袋；A未改营地规则。

units.title: 初三阅读：旅舍行李牌的两条信息

materials.title: Hostel Luggage Labels
materials.text:
Our school group reached a youth hostel before the rooms were ready. The receptionist offered to keep our bags in a store room while we visited the town. Each bag needed a label with the owner's name and the group number. I wrote only my first name because I thought everyone knew me.

When we came back, another school group was waiting in the entrance. One of its members had the same first name as me and a similar dark suitcase. The receptionist did not let either of us choose a bag from appearance alone. She asked us to describe a detail that was not visible from across the room and checked our group lists.

My suitcase had a small green patch beside the lower handle. The other student's had a broken zip pocket on the front. Once the bags were identified, we added the missing group information to the labels.

I had treated the label as a note for my friends. In fact, it was also a message for people who did not know me and for a situation in which another group might arrive. The extra line had seemed unnecessary only because I had imagined the hostel store room as an extension of our own classroom.

questions.prompt: Why were the bags placed in a store room?
options: The suitcases were all too small for the bedrooms.
The hostel did not allow anyone to bring clothes.
The rooms were not ready when the group arrived.
The students had decided to throw them away.
questions.explanation: C正确：早到房未备；D非弃物；B允许衣物；A未说尺寸问题。

questions.prompt: What information had the narrator omitted?
options: The name of the town.
The group number.
The first name.
The colour of the receptionist’s desk.
questions.explanation: B正确：只写名漏组号；C名已写；A镇名非所需标签；D桌色无关。

questions.prompt: How were the similar suitcases identified?
options: By whichever student reached them first.
By checking specific details and the group lists.
By assuming both bags belonged to one group.
By first names alone.
questions.explanation: B正确：问细节并查名单；A不抢先；D重名不足；C两团不能假同。

questions.prompt: Which detail identified the narrator’s bag?
options: A broken front zip pocket.
A green patch by the lower handle.
A large yellow school flag.
A missing wheel on every side.
questions.explanation: B正确：低柄旁绿补丁；A是另一人；C旗、D多轮丢失无据。

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the final paragraph?
options: Everyone with the same name must own identical luggage.
A label is only useful among close friends.
The hostel should never store bags for guests.
Instructions should account for readers and situations beyond one’s own group.
questions.explanation: D正确：标签给不认识自己者、另一团到来场景用；B作者纠正此旧观；C未否存包；A同名仍有不同细节。

units.title: 初三阅读：视频交流中的两个星期五

materials.title: Penpal Video Time
materials.text:
Our class arranged a video call with a partner school overseas. The invitation said “Friday afternoon”, and we immediately began planning a classroom activity. It was only when the teachers compared their schedules that we noticed a problem: Friday afternoon for one school was already a different time of day for the other.

Our teacher showed us both local times on one shared plan. We did not need to memorise a rule about every country. We needed to know exactly when this particular call would happen at each end. The plan also included the date, because a day name alone could hide the difference.

The change affected the activity. One class would be near the end of its school day, while the other would be starting. We shortened the introductions and sent some questions in advance. This gave both groups something useful to prepare without expecting them to have the same amount of free time immediately beforehand.

On the call, a pupil from the partner school thanked us for writing the times clearly. I had thought “Friday afternoon” was a friendly, simple phrase. It was friendly, but it was not complete until the reader knew whose Friday afternoon it referred to.

options: An invitation used a day and part of the day without making both local times clear.
The two schools spoke on different planets.
Nobody knew the name of Friday.
The teachers had refused to compare schedules.
questions.explanation: A正确：Friday afternoon依当地时间不同；B非星球；C不是不知星期词；D老师正比日程发现。

questions.prompt: What did the shared plan show?
options: Only the narrator’s lunch menu.
A rule that all clocks must be identical.
Every country’s history.
The exact date and local time for both schools.
questions.explanation: D正确：列两地具体时与日期；A菜单、C历史、B全钟同刻不是计划。

questions.prompt: Why were some questions sent in advance?
options: To support preparation despite different schedules around the call.
To make the partner school prepare the whole event alone.
To replace the call without telling anyone.
To stop anyone asking questions during the call.
questions.explanation: A正确：两端课日前后可准备时不同，预发有助；D未禁问；B非全推；C通话仍有。

options: They became longer than the whole school day.
They were spoken only by the teachers.
They were shortened.
They were removed from every future lesson.
questions.explanation: C正确：shortened introductions；D非永删；A非超日；B未限老师。

questions.prompt: What does the narrator conclude about “Friday afternoon”?
options: Its meaning in this invitation depended on the reader’s location.
It should never be used in any conversation.
It was an unfriendly expression.
It always described exactly the same moment worldwide.
questions.explanation: A正确：需明谁的周五下午；C友好未否；B非全禁用；D恰相反。

units.title: 初三阅读：二手校服上不同的说明

materials.title: Uniform Sale Condition
materials.text:
At our school's second-hand uniform sale, clothes were first arranged by size. This helped people find a starting point, but a parent asked why two jackets with the same size label fitted differently. One had been shortened by its previous owner.

The volunteers added a place on each price card for changes and condition notes. A repaired pocket, a shorter sleeve or a missing button could matter to the next wearer. The notes did not automatically make an item undesirable. One student was delighted to find a jacket with shorter sleeves because that was exactly what she needed.

We also left time for trying clothes on. A size label was useful information, not a promise of a perfect fit. Volunteers could explain the notes, but they did not tell every buyer that the largest available size would be the safest choice.

At the end of the sale, my classmate said that the condition cards made the clothes look less perfect. I thought they made the sale more useful. A careful description allowed an item to be chosen for the person who would actually use it, rather than for an imagined buyer who needed everything to be unchanged.

questions.prompt: Why did the two jackets with the same size label fit differently?
options: They had both been made of paper.
The volunteers had hidden every smaller jacket.
One had been altered by its former owner.
Their labels described the school’s address.
questions.explanation: C正确：一件原主改短；A非纸衣；D标签是尺码非地址；B未藏小号。

questions.prompt: What was added to the price cards?
options: Only the colour of the school building.
A promise never to repair anything.
Notes about changes and condition.
A list of every former student.
questions.explanation: C正确：改动现状说明；D学生全名单、B禁修承诺、A楼色非内容。

questions.prompt: Why was a shorter sleeve not necessarily a disadvantage?
options: All jackets had to be shortened again.
Nobody at the sale had arms.
It could match a particular buyer’s needs.
The size labels were all removed.
questions.explanation: C正确：有学生正需短袖长；B荒谬；D尺码仍有；A非全改短。

questions.prompt: How was a size label treated?
options: As an instruction to buy the largest size.
As proof of the jacket’s price when new.
As a guarantee that no fitting was needed.
As useful information that did not replace trying the item on.
questions.explanation: D正确：尺码有用但非完美合身保证，留试穿；C、A相反；B非原价证明。

questions.prompt: Why did the narrator prefer the condition cards?
options: They supported a choice based on the actual wearer and item.
They made every jacket look new.
They prevented anyone buying altered clothes.
They removed all differences between items.
questions.explanation: A正确：具体衣物适具体人；B不装新；C允许买改过；D揭示差异非抹掉。

units.title: 初三阅读：免费活动为什么仍需预约

materials.title: Free Event Booking
materials.text:
Our town museum advertised a free evening of short talks. The large poster said “Everyone welcome”, but a smaller line asked people to book a seat. I assumed that free meant I could arrive whenever I liked without contacting anyone.

My older sister read the full notice. The talks were free of charge, but the room held only a limited audience. Booking did not mean buying a ticket. It allowed the museum to avoid promising more seats than it had. We reserved two places online and received a message telling us when to arrive.

At the entrance, a visitor without a booking asked whether the museum had changed the price. A volunteer explained that no payment was required. There were a few spare seats because some booked visitors had cancelled, and the volunteer checked the list before admitting anyone else.

After the talks, I looked at the poster again. “Free” answered a question about cost, not every question about how to attend. The notice might have been clearer with a larger booking instruction, but I had also filled the gap with an assumption that the word itself did not support.

questions.prompt: What did the narrator initially assume?
options: Booking required buying several talks at once.
The museum had no room for talks.
Everyone had already cancelled.
A free event needed no contact or booking.
questions.explanation: D正确：以为免费即可任意到；A非其初猜；B有有限座房；C部分取消非全。

questions.prompt: Why did the museum request bookings?
options: To manage a limited number of places.
To make the talks longer.
To stop local people attending.
To secretly charge for every seat.
questions.explanation: A正确：容量有限避免超许座；D没收款；C欢迎大家非禁本地；B非延时。

questions.prompt: Why were some unbooked visitors admitted?
options: Every booked visitor had paid twice.
The room suddenly became unlimited.
The volunteer threw away the list.
Cancellations had left spare seats.
questions.explanation: D正确：取消产生空座核表后放；B容量没变；C查名单；A无付款。

options: Whether a charge was required.
Exactly when every guest would arrive.
Which volunteer knew the narrator.
Whether every possible visitor had a seat.
questions.explanation: A正确：免费指费用；B到时、D座保证、C关系非该词义。

questions.prompt: What is the narrator’s final view?
options: Booking always means that an event is no longer free.
The notice could be clearer, and the narrator had also made an unsupported assumption.
No instruction should accompany a free event.
Only the museum was responsible for every misunderstanding.
questions.explanation: B正确：可放大预约说明，同时自己擅补免费含义；D非全归馆；C仍需规则；A预约不等收费。

units.title: 初三阅读：试演时备用的那份台词

materials.title: Audition Prompt Copy
materials.text:
I wanted the main part in our school play and spent a week practising the opening speech. At the audition, I missed a line and could not find my place. The director asked me to begin again, but I was already thinking about the mistake rather than the scene.

I did not get the main part. Instead, I was offered a small role and asked whether I could help prepare a prompt copy of the script. I first heard the request as a polite way to keep me busy. Then the director showed me what the job involved: marking entrances, checking changed lines and recording where a scene had been shortened.

At rehearsal, the student with the main part stopped at exactly the line I had forgotten. I could point to the right place because I had checked the revised script. He thanked me and asked about another change. We began discussing the scene rather than comparing our auditions.

I still wished I had performed better, and the small role did not suddenly become my dream. However, the script work gave me a clearer understanding of the whole play. At the final rehearsal, I brought two copies: one for my own lines and one whose careful notes could help someone else find a way through theirs.

questions.prompt: What made the second attempt at the audition difficult?
options: The director had removed every line from the script.
The school had cancelled the play.
The main actor was already performing on stage.
The narrator was thinking about the earlier mistake.
questions.explanation: D正确：已专注失误非场景；A未清空剧本；C主角当时未定；B戏仍排演。

questions.prompt: How did the narrator first interpret the prompt-copy request?
options: As an invitation to direct every scene alone.
As a polite task mainly intended to keep them occupied.
As proof that the main role had been awarded after all.
As a demand to stop acting permanently.
questions.explanation: B正确：初听像客气安排让忙；C没获主角；A非独导；D仍小角色。

questions.prompt: Why could the narrator help the main actor at rehearsal?
options: The director had asked everyone to forget the opening.
The narrator had checked the revised script and its changes.
The narrator had secretly changed the audition result.
The actor had never read any script.
questions.explanation: B正确：检查新版故能定位；C未改选角；D非从没读；A未要忘词。

questions.prompt: Which feeling remains at the end?
options: A wish to cancel all small roles.
Anger that nobody had ever thanked the narrator.
Regret about the audition alongside a new understanding of the play.
A belief that the narrator never wanted the main part.
questions.explanation: C正确：仍wish performedbetter且理解全剧；D仍想主角；A不取消；B演员已感谢。

questions.prompt: What do the two script copies suggest?
options: The notes are no longer useful at rehearsal.
The narrator plans to replace every actor.
Only the narrator’s own lines matter.
The narrator now prepares both for a personal role and for helping others.
questions.explanation: D正确：一自用一助他人，双重准备；B非换全员；C不只自己；A笔记有效。

units.title: 初三阅读：邮戳不能证明照片拍摄日

materials.title: Postmark Photo Date
materials.text:
For a class display about our street, I found a postcard showing a shop that had closed long before I was born. The back had a clear postmark from 1991. I wrote “Our street in 1991” beneath the picture and felt pleased to have an exact date.

A neighbour who saw the draft asked why I had chosen that year. When I showed her the postmark, she explained that it dated the sending of the card, not necessarily the taking of the photograph. A card could remain in a shop for several years before someone bought and posted it.

We looked more closely at the image. A bus stop sign stood where the neighbour remembered a later bus shelter. Her memory suggested another question, but it was not enough on its own to establish a new date. I asked the local library whether it had a record of when the shelter was built.

The record helped narrow the period, although we still could not identify the photographer's exact day. My final caption explained both the likely range and the 1991 postmark. It was less neat than a single year, but readers could see what each piece of information actually supported.

questions.prompt: Why did the narrator originally choose 1991?
options: It appeared in the postmark.
It was printed as the photographer’s name.
The narrator remembered visiting the shop that year.
The class required every image to be dated 1991.
questions.explanation: A正确：邮戳1991；B非姓名；C作者未出生不自忆；D无统一年份规则。

questions.prompt: What distinction did the neighbour explain?
options: The age of every person on the street.
A stamp price and the cost of a photograph.
Shop opening hours and bus fares.
The date a card was sent and the date its picture was taken.
questions.explanation: D正确：寄出与拍照日期不同；C/B/A非核心区别。

questions.prompt: How was the neighbour’s memory treated?
options: As a reason to destroy the postcard.
As proof that the shop had never existed.
As an exact replacement date requiring no checks.
As a clue that led to a further question.
questions.explanation: D正确：记忆引新问题需图书馆核查；C不单靠记忆定年；A未毁；B商店确有。

questions.prompt: What did the library record help establish?
options: That postmarks always date photographs.
The photographer’s exact day with certainty.
A narrower possible period for the image.
The name of every bus passenger.
questions.explanation: C正确：收窄时期但非具体日；B明确不能；D无乘客名；A戳不是拍日。

questions.prompt: Why was the final caption useful despite being less simple?
options: It showed the different support provided by the date range and postmark.
It claimed the neighbour’s memory was always wrong.
It removed the image from the street’s history.
It hid every uncertain detail.
questions.explanation: A正确：让读者明各证据支撑何事；D公开范围；C仍街史展；B没有总否邻居。

units.title: 初三阅读：食谱里不是同一只杯子

materials.title: Recipe Cup Measure
materials.text:
My cousin sent me a cake recipe she had used while staying with a family overseas. The ingredient list said “two cups of flour”. I took two large tea cups from our cupboard and filled them. The mixture became much thicker than my cousin had described.

I called her before adding more liquid. She asked what kind of cup I had used. I said it was the one I normally drank tea from. She explained that her recipe used a measuring cup, not any cup that happened to be in a kitchen. The word was familiar, but the quantity behind it had not been clear to me.

We checked the recipe's notes and found measurements by weight as well. I could not remove flour neatly from the mixture I had already made, so I asked an experienced adult for help rather than guessing at several further changes. For the next attempt, we prepared the ingredients using the stated weights.

The second cake was much closer to the result we expected. In my recipe notebook, I added a note about the measuring cup and kept the weight information. I had not needed a more unusual word; I had needed a more precise understanding of an ordinary one.

questions.prompt: What did the narrator use for the first attempt?
options: The recipe’s standard measuring cup.
The cousin’s overseas family kitchen.
A set of scales for every ingredient.
Large tea cups from home.
questions.explanation: D正确：用家里大茶杯；A非量杯；C未先按重；B在自家。

questions.prompt: What was the first sign of a problem?
options: The mixture was much thicker than expected.
The cousin refused to answer the phone.
Every cup had disappeared.
The recipe had no ingredient list.
questions.explanation: A正确：面糊过稠；D有清单；B接电话；C杯都在。

questions.prompt: What did “cup” mean in the cousin’s recipe?
options: A specified measuring cup.
Any container used for tea.
A request to buy matching plates.
The total size of the finished cake.
questions.explanation: A正确：标准量杯非任意茶杯；B原误会；D成品大小、C买盘无关。

questions.prompt: What helped make the next attempt more controlled?
options: Guessing several extra changes at once.
Ignoring the notes to save time.
Using a still larger tea cup.
Following the weight measurements in the notes.
questions.explanation: D正确：查重量按指定备料；A避免乱补；B保留读注；C非更大茶杯。

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence emphasise?
options: Only unusual words cause communication problems.
A successful cake requires no measurements.
An ordinary word can need a precise meaning in a particular task.
Every recipe from another place must be wrong.
questions.explanation: C正确：熟词cup量义需准；A非只生词；D配方未错；B测量正重要。

units.title: 初三阅读：采访文字稿中的两个相似名字

materials.title: Interview Transcript Name
materials.text:
Our class interviewed a local gardener for the school magazine. I helped turn the recording into a written article. The gardener mentioned two volunteers, Anna and Ana, who had worked on different parts of the garden. Listening quickly, I thought she was referring to one person and combined their actions in a paragraph.

Before publication, our teacher asked the gardener to check the article. She marked the paragraph and explained the two spellings. Anna had organised the tools; Ana had designed a sign. The difference was small on the page but important to the people whose work was being described.

I checked the recording again. It helped me locate the sentence, but sound alone did not settle the spelling. We asked the gardener to confirm the names in writing. Then I separated the two accounts and sent the corrected paragraph back for a final check.

In our class notes, I wrote that turning speech into print was not just typing faster. Some details needed a different kind of confirmation. The article became clearer because we asked rather than because I became more confident in my first guess.

questions.prompt: What mistake did the narrator make?
options: Recorded only the sound of the tools.
Removed every mention of the gardener.
Refused to write any names.
Treated two volunteers as one person.
questions.explanation: D正确：将Anna/Ana两人行动合一；B仍采访园丁；A录访谈；C写了误名。

questions.prompt: How did the mistake come to light?
options: The narrator counted all garden tools.
The gardener checked the article before publication.
A new camera changed the recording.
The two names were printed on every classroom desk.
questions.explanation: B正确：发表前受访者校稿指出；C相机、A数工具、D桌名无据。

questions.prompt: Why was listening again insufficient by itself?
options: It did not establish the spelling of the similar names.
There was no sentence about either volunteer.
Sound could never provide any useful information.
The recording had been completely erased.
questions.explanation: A正确：声音可定位句但不确定拼法；D仍录音；B有提；C仍有用非全无。

questions.prompt: What did the class do to confirm the detail?
options: Removed both volunteers from the article.
Used the same name twice to avoid questions.
Chose the spelling that looked prettier.
Asked for the names in writing.
questions.explanation: D正确：请园丁书面确认；C美观非据；A未删功；B正要区分。

options: Some spoken details need confirmation in another form.
A confident guess is always better than asking.
Typing speed is the only important skill in writing an interview.
Every small spelling difference changes the entire story.
questions.explanation: A正确：信息需不同形式核实；C不是仅速度；B问才清；D不全盘夸每微差改全故事。

units.title: 初三阅读：读到一半时写的书评

materials.title: Unfinished Book Review
materials.text:
For our class website, I began writing a review of a novel after reading only half of it. The opening chapters followed a character who kept making promises and failing to keep them. I wrote that the author did not understand how a believable person would behave.

My friend read the draft and asked whether the repeated broken promises might be part of the story's purpose. I thought she was defending a book she liked. She said I did not have to like it, but I should know what happened before deciding that a pattern was simply a mistake.

I finished the novel over the weekend. The later chapters did not make me admire the character, but they showed consequences that my first draft had assumed were absent. I changed the review. It still criticised some scenes, yet it now described what the book had actually done rather than what I had expected it to do halfway through.

The teacher suggested keeping the early draft in my folder. It showed a real first response, but it was not the same as a considered review of the complete work. I had learned to preserve an impression without giving it more authority than the reading behind it could support.

questions.prompt: When did the narrator write the first draft?
options: After reading about half of the novel.
Only after the author visited the school.
After reading every chapter twice.
Before opening the novel.
questions.explanation: A正确：读半开始评；C非读完两遍；D已有阅读；B无作者访问。

options: The pattern might be intentional, so the narrator should read on before judging it.
The review should be deleted without finishing the book.
Broken promises could never be meaningful in fiction.
The narrator had to praise the novel.
questions.explanation: A正确：可能有意安排，读完再判；D说不必喜欢；C恰相反；B未让直接删。

questions.prompt: What did the later chapters change?
options: They removed the opening chapters from the book.
They revealed consequences the draft had assumed were missing.
They made the narrator admire every character.
They proved that criticism was forbidden.
questions.explanation: B正确：后果原被假定无；C仍不钦角色；D仍批部分场景；A开篇未删。

questions.prompt: Why did the final review still contain criticism?
options: The teacher demanded an entirely negative review.
Finishing the book informed the judgement without requiring praise.
The narrator had refused to read the ending.
The friend had changed every sentence secretly.
questions.explanation: B正确：充分阅读使批评据全书，不强赞；C读完；A非全负；D未代改。

questions.prompt: Why was the early draft worth keeping?
options: It recorded a genuine initial response with a more limited basis.
It could replace reading any future book.
It proved first impressions never change.
It was the most complete account of the whole novel.
questions.explanation: A正确：真实首反应但不同完整审慎书评；D基础半本；C已变；B不能代读。
